extracted.intended_audience: trust and safety professionals, platform moderators, researchers, and policy makers
extracted.subtask_description: A case-study style analysis of Reddit's June 2023 site-wide moderator 'blackout' in response to API pricing changes, intended to surface lessons for trust & safety, platform governance, and corporate decision-making. Focuses on moderators, third-party apps, corporate responses, and broader implications for LLM/data use and platform regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of volunteer moderators
rubrics_metrics.description: Reddit’s moderators uphold Reddit’s Content Policy and ensure the well-being of their respective subreddits; they are volunteers who spend approximately 466 cumulative unpaid labor hours every day to maintain their communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize moderators as essential, unpaid labor sustaining platform communities; evaluate policy or product changes (e.g., API pricing) for their impact on volunteer workload and community health. Example: large subreddits require extensive moderator effort that third‑party tools help manage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependence on third-party apps for moderation and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Third-party apps provide essential services—help moderators organize subreddits, block accounts, flag unsafe posts, find patterns of abuse, communicate with the moderation team, provide mobile access, and accessibility for visual- and hearing-impaired users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess platform functionality gaps and how third-party tools fill them; consider that charging for API access can remove tools critical for moderation and accessibility. Example: Reddit lacked official moderation tools and only released an official mobile app in 2016.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for API pricing (company justification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reddit announced it would begin charging companies for API use because it needs to be 'self-sustaining' and 'can no longer subsidize commercial entities that require large-scale data use'—specifically referencing LLMs trained on Reddit data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating company policy, weigh stated financial/sustainability rationales against downstream community and moderation impacts. Consider transparency of rationale and whether alternatives or exemptions are justified (e.g., accessibility apps were exempt).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of API pricing on third-party apps and user tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed pricing ($12,000 per 50 million API requests) caused popular third-party apps like Apollo to announce shutdowns, making some apps face ~ $20M/year costs and resulting in closures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure direct operational/financial effects on app developers, loss of moderator/admin tools, and indirect harms to users (e.g., accessibility loss). Example consequences noted: app shutdowns, decreased Google search quality, and site instability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness and characteristics of collective moderator action
rubrics_metrics.description: Over 8,829 subreddits pledged to 'go dark' (go private) June 12-14 to protest the API changes; this is an act of 'sabotage' intended to make visible moderators' demands and stop the update that removes moderator tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat coordinated moderator actions (going dark, prolonged dark periods, NSFW tagging, malicious compliance) as powerful levers that can disrupt platform operation and visibility. Examples: site crashes, declines in search quality, and extended attrition strategies where thousands of subreddits remained dark after the initial blackout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tactics moderators may use and their trade-offs
rubrics_metrics.description: Moderators used strategies including making subreddits private ('going dark'), tagging as NSFW to block ad revenue, malicious compliance (e.g., reopening but posting satirical content), and sustained attrition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When anticipating or evaluating protests, catalog likely tactics and their effects (ad revenue loss, reinstatements, moderator suspensions). Example: r/pics and r/aww reopened with only photos of John Oliver; NSFW tagging led to moderator suspensions and later reinstatements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate response and communication tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Reddit CEO Steve Huffman publicly criticized moderators, suggested volunteers were abusing privileges, compared them to 'landed gentry', and proposed strategies that might remove moderators—leading to a 'flame war'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate corporate messaging and escalation choices; aggressive or dismissive public responses can inflame conflicts and damage trust. Consider alternative communication strategies to de‑escalate and negotiate with volunteer communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risks of enforcement actions and moderator replacement
rubrics_metrics.description: Some communities were forced reopened by Administrators after moderator teams were replaced; moderator teams were suspended and later reinstated in some cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the long-term community and reputational costs of forcibly replacing moderators or applying top-down enforcement; forced reopenings can spur community exits and erosion of trust between users and the company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader platform harms and externalities
rubrics_metrics.description: The blackout produced site crashes, reduced quality of Google search results, and sparked journalists to declare an 'end of the useful internet'; ransomware threats to leak hacked data also arose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify systemic harms beyond immediate community disruption—searchability, platform reliability, security threats, and public perception. Use these externalities to inform cost–benefit analysis of product/policy changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visibility and power of trust and safety workers
rubrics_metrics.description: The blackout highlights how trust and safety workers (including volunteers) have collective power to influence platforms; both the 2015 and 2023 blackouts show instances of collective action among these workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate the organized capacity of trust & safety actors into governance planning—recognize their role in shaping platform behavior and design engagement processes that include them as stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity cost of allowing LLM companies to mine text data
rubrics_metrics.description: Company consideration: 'What is the opportunity cost of allowing LLM companies to mine large amounts of text data? Is it equivalent to the amount being proposed for API calls?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the trade-off between monetizing API access and the societal/operational value of keeping data broadly available for developers, researchers, and accessibility. Consider non-monetary values (public benefit, research, moderation capacity) when pricing access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentive structures for volunteer moderators and third‑party developers
rubrics_metrics.description: Company consideration: 'What incentivizes volunteer moderators and third-party app developers to contribute without expecting pay? Do such actions undermine that incentive?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether policies (e.g., monetizing APIs) disincentivize unpaid contributions; consider creating incentives or compensations, and evaluate whether removing tools undermines volunteer motivation and community stewardship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community vs corporate identity and reconciliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Company consideration: 'Can a distinction be made between Reddit as a community of users and Reddit as a corporate entity? If so, how can they be reconciled?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing policy, explicitly analyze the dual roles of platform as a business and as an ecosystem of communities. Consider governance models or mechanisms to reconcile competing objectives (community autonomy vs corporate sustainability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory framing: should social platforms be utilities or public goods?
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue consideration: 'Given their importance in the modern era, should social media sites like Reddit be considered a utility or public good and regulated as such?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame policy evaluation in light of potential regulation—assess whether critical functions served by platforms justify regulatory treatment, and consider implications for platform obligations, access, and pricing models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderator rights to speak and act on behalf of communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue consideration: 'Do moderators have a right to speak and take action on behalf of the communities they oversee?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze normative and legal dimensions of moderator authority and representation; consider formalizing moderator rights, responsibilities, and channels for dispute/resolution between moderators and platform governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry trend: impacts of rising API pricing across platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue consideration: 'Both Twitter and Reddit have significantly increased API pricing—what are the potential impacts of this trend? Will the user and moderator responses towards these actions lead to new platforms gaining ground?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate cross-platform trends and market effects: developer ecosystem contraction, migration to alternative platforms, and potential emergence of new competitors. Use scenario analysis to predict user migration and platform evolution.
